sample_unit: participants (102 OVCF, 102 controls); external validation n=56

links.outcome: Internal-to-external AUC degradation on geographically independent validation cohort
links.effect: External validation (n=56) Gradient Boosting AUC 0.838 (95% CI 0.712–0.940), sensitivity 89.3%, specificity 71.4%, with negligible internal-to-external AUC degradation (ΔAUC < 0.001).
links.quote: On geographically independent external validation ( n = 56), the Gradient Boosting model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.838 (95% CI: 0.712–0.940), sensitivity of 89.3%, and specificity of 71.4%, with negligible internal-to-external AUC degradation (ΔAUC < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Post-hoc isotonic recalibration to reduce miscalibration in extreme-probability tails
Score–explanation concordance analysis of LLM-generated scores and explanations

screen.reason: The study develops and externally validates a multimodal LLM framework for triage of vertebral fractures, and explicitly tests post-hoc isotonic recalibration to mitigate extreme-probability miscalibration.
